findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - a Codex builder must run its failing regression through forge test during a work round.
The named proof checks outgoing approval settings but never executes forge test. Its app-server stub requests marker-file operations and fabricates failed pytest output (tests/stubs/codex-app-server:57–64,224–229). The existing live smoke uses read-only turns (tests/test_codex_smoke.py:69–72), so it cannot supply the missing worker execution proof. These checks can pass without demonstrating the Done-when behavior. Add a worker-round regression that actually invokes forge test and observes the expected test failure without a permission refusal.
findings.title: Not done: A Codex builder runs forge test in its round without a permission refusal.

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Gate
Case: normal use - an existing client upgrades Forge and starts a Codex worker round.
The repository requires each changed rule to retain at least one case on a client adopted on an earlier release. This regression uses _codex_repo's default forge-source setup (tests/test_codex_worker.py:113–133); the listed design-route proof uses a newly configured client (tests/test_design_route.py:121), and none of the listed approval proofs exercises an earlier-adopted client. Extend the approval contract's primary test with one earlier-release client case so the claimed upgrade behavior is covered.
findings.title: Gate: worker approval coverage for earlier-adopted clients

why: Codex builders must write a failing test and watch it fail with forge test, but the refusal blocks that step, so the item reaches CI without that check.
